The folder-side pending row (a provisional root group) is covered by the earlier projection change and not re-driven here. Displayed state is the production projection and window decision, not a rendered view. It runs in an unsigned swift test process with a stub bookmark codec.

gates.normative_summary: Direct icon drop. One or many original files, supported content, promises, and mixed files and folders each open the correct review exactly once. No original bytes or attributes are mutated by capture.
gates.applicability: macOS 13 or later, signed installed companion with a live status item receiving real drag sessions.

evidence.covers: One drag session reaches review exactly once.
Promised files are reported once, in the order the source promised them.
A mixed file and folder drop is classified in the order given.
Original bytes and attributes are unchanged by a capture run.

gates.missing_condition: Section 20.1 requires evidence in an installed signed build. The packaging manifest records the candidate as unsigned and not release eligible, no drag session is ever performed, and StatusItemDropView has no test.
gates.limitations: The drag policy is proven as a pure function over declared pasteboard types and counts. Nothing exercises NSDraggingDestination, the status button's child view, or a real promise provider.

gates.normative_summary: Native status behaviour. Left and right click, keyboard activation, VoiceOver, Command-drag reorder and removal, opening the menu, hover exit and subsequent clicks all retain correct behaviour with the drop adapter installed.
gates.applicability: macOS 13 or later installed companion status item with the transparent drop child attached.

evidence.covers: The hover affordance delay, which is the timing the hover-exit behaviour depends on.

gates.missing_condition: Every condition this gate lists is an input event delivered by the window server to an installed status item. No click, keypress, Command-drag or VoiceOver interaction is performed anywhere in the repository, and there is no accessibility test of any kind.
gates.limitations: Only one timing constant is covered. The gate's whole point, that the adapter does not break the status item's native behaviour, is untested in every respect.

gates.normative_summary: Display and accessibility. A hidden menu bar, fullscreen, multiple displays, display removal, a near-edge icon, Dark Mode, Reduce Motion and text scaling all leave no unreachable or orphan UI.
gates.applicability: macOS 13 or later installed companion across every supported display and appearance configuration.

evidence.covers: The near-edge clamp keeps the affordance inside the visible screen frame.

gates.missing_condition: There is no visual, appearance, Reduce Motion, text-scaling or multi-display test anywhere, and no accessibility qualification record. The clamp is the only piece with coverage, and it is exercised against injected rectangles rather than real screens.
gates.limitations: One geometric helper, with synthetic input. Nothing shows what happens when a display is removed while the affordance is on it, which is the orphan-UI case the gate names.

gates.normative_summary: Drag operation semantics. Copy-permitted sources work and move-only sources are rejected. Modifier keys never convert ingestion into source mutation.
gates.applicability: macOS 13 or later installed companion status item receiving real drag sessions with and without modifier keys.

evidence.covers: The drop route's admission decision, which is where the returned operation is chosen.
Capture does not mutate the source, which is the consequence a modifier key must not be able to change.

gates.missing_condition: No test asserts the returned NSDragOperation is copy, and no test supplies a move-only source or a modifier key. The README states the view returns copy only; nothing checks it, and a real drag session is required to observe what the source then does.
gates.limitations: The policy that decides admission is covered. The operation it reports back to the drag source, which is the entire subject of this gate, is not asserted anywhere.

gates.normative_summary: File promises. Export failure, cancellation, capacity exhaustion and producer termination create truthful rows and no queued acknowledgement. Completed owned bytes survive provider expiry.
gates.applicability: macOS 13 or later installed companion receiving real NSFilePromiseReceiver deliveries.

evidence.covers: A failed promise settles and is not reported as delivered.
Producer termination is bounded by the delivery timeout and late callbacks are ignored.
A provider that overruns its declared size or misnames its file settles nothing.
Completed owned bytes survive the source going away.

gates.missing_condition: Section 20.1 requires an installed signed build. The promise state machine is driven by a test harness standing in for NSFilePromiseReceiver, so no real producer ever exports, cancels or dies, and no queued acknowledgement is observed being withheld by the real queue.
gates.limitations: The failure, timeout and overrun paths are covered well as pure state transitions on a temporary directory. Capacity exhaustion is covered on the quota side rather than from a promise, and the truthful-rows half is a projection no test reads.

gates.normative_summary: Native Quick Action preservation. An installed viewer-role action appears for the intended single and multiple files and directories. Success, handoff, cancel, error and host termination all leave original Finder URLs, bytes and attributes unchanged.
gates.applicability: macOS 13 or later, signed installed Finder Action extension macOS has registered.

evidence.covers: Writes the NSExtension block and activation rule for the com.apple.ui-services Action extension into the generated plist.
The packaged app embeds real Finder Action and Share appex bundles under Contents/PlugIns.
The extension completes only once every offered slot is adopted.
A mixed file and directory selection keeps its order and acknowledges only after every adoption.

gates.missing_condition: FinderActionViewController is not a Swift Package target and has no tests; its sources are only typechecked under -application-extension, never run, by the macOS row of the Phase 2 platform workflow and by the local Darwin preflight. Whether the action appears in Finder for the intended selections can only be observed on a signed installed build macOS has registered, and no signed build exists.
gates.limitations: The companion side of the handoff is covered well. The extension that returns the NSExtensionItem objects unmodified, which is the preservation claim, has no automated coverage at all.

gates.normative_summary: Representation identity. Actual Finder originals, local-copy providers, exports and preview-text alternatives each take their specified routes. No temporary path becomes a linked original.
gates.applicability: macOS 13 or later installed companion across the Finder, Share, drop and Shortcuts routes.

evidence.covers: Alternative representations of one logical item collapse to one slot in a fixed preference order.
The fixed representation preference order, so a preview-text alternative cannot displace the real payload.
A snapshot never acquires an original binding, so a temporary path cannot become a linked original.
Each surface keeps its own provenance through review, which is the routes-stay-distinct requirement.

gates.missing_condition: The representations the gate distinguishes are supplied by real NSItemProvider instances from real host applications. Every test constructs them directly, so nothing shows a genuine local-copy provider or export being classified, and an installed signed build is required to receive one.
gates.limitations: The classification rules and the no-temporary-original invariant are covered directly and are strong. Their inputs are synthetic, so the mapping from a real provider to a route is untested.

gates.normative_summary: Access handoff. A real implicit transfer is resolved while valid, and only companion-created persistent access survives restart. Copied explicit extension bookmarks, expired tokens and forged peer claims all fail safely.
gates.applicability: macOS 13 or later, signed installed companion and extensions sharing an App Group, with real security-scoped bookmarks and real code-signing identities.

evidence.covers: Expired, mismatched and traversal offers are rejected.
The peer requirement rejects invalid inputs.
A companion-created grant persists owner-only and balances its access, which is the survives-restart half.
The peer socket reports the kernel's own peer uid and pid rather than a claimed identity.

gates.missing_condition: Two mechanisms this gate rests on are never exercised. Every test substitutes a stub bookmark codec encoding the path as Data(url.path.utf8), so SystemSecurityScopedBookmarkCodec and real implicit transfer resolution are untested. Peer verification is covered only on its input-validation path: designatedRequirement, SecCodeCheckValidity against a signed peer, and NativeHandoffPeerServer rejection have no test, and a forged peer claim cannot be constructed without signed identities.
gates.limitations: The mailbox nonce, expiry and traversal rules are well covered, and the socket does report real kernel peer identity, but for an unsigned test process. The copied-explicit-bookmark case cannot even be represented while the codec is a path string.

gates.normative_summary: Cold companion. Actual Action and Share targets can use the chosen supported activation path where advertised, and launch failure or manual continuation is truthful. No second companion or Core authority appears.
gates.applicability: macOS 13 or later, signed installed extensions activating a companion that is not running.

evidence.covers: A request made while the companion was closed is adopted at startup, which is the manual-continuation path.
A second launch forwards one fixed intent and exits, so no second companion appears.

gates.missing_condition: Activation of a non-running companion by an extension requires macOS to have registered that extension from a signed installed build. No test launches a process from an extension, and the truthfulness of the launch-failure wording is not asserted anywhere.
gates.limitations: Durable continuation while closed and the single-instance rule are both covered. The activation attempt itself, which is what the gate is about, is not performed.

gates.normative_summary: Lost handoff acknowledgement. The same request and slot-to-candidate mapping recovers without duplicate drafts, grants or captures. An existing draft permits prompt waiting-queue adoption, and no Core destination is required before Add. Destination changes, transfer expiry, candidate lifetime and cancel or publication ownership follow their separate boundaries.
gates.applicability: macOS 13 or later companion and extensions sharing the App Group handoff mailbox.

evidence.covers: A lost acknowledgement reconciles against the same adoption rather than creating a second.
The Share route recovers without copying the bytes again.
An exact replay maps to the same refs and adopts once, which is the slot-to-candidate mapping requirement.
Failure injected at every boundary converges on the same adoption.
Candidate lifetime is independent of the transfer window, which is one of the separate boundaries.

gates.missing_condition: Section 20.1 requires an installed signed build. The recovery logic is exercised exhaustively, but both participants are the same test process against a temporary directory, with no App Group, no extension and no real transfer expiry clock.
gates.limitations: This is the best-covered native gate in the repository and the convergence properties are genuinely strong. What is untested is that a real extension and a real companion, in two processes under macOS extension lifetime rules, reach the same convergence.

gates.normative_summary: Folder picker and drop. Add current files and Watch folder mode, and recursion and exclusions, are explicit. Package and alias escape and out-of-root locators are denied. Over-limit scope produces no silent partial enrolment.
gates.applicability: macOS 13 or later installed companion folder picker and folder drop routes.

evidence.covers: An over-limit scope is refused and enrols nothing, so there is no silent partial enrolment.
Packages and bundles are neither descended into nor accepted.
Symlinks and Finder aliases are never followed, which is the escape denial.
Recursion off never lists a subfolder, so recursion is explicit rather than advisory.
The folder picker policy is fixed to one directory and no file.

gates.missing_condition: Section 20.1 requires an installed signed build. No NSOpenPanel is presented and no folder drop is performed, so the two routes the gate names are never driven; only the scope policy behind them is exercised.
gates.limitations: Scope, recursion, exclusion and escape denial are covered thoroughly against real temporary directory trees. Mode selection is covered as a policy value, and the two entry routes are not exercised at all.

gates.normative_summary: Frozen import membership. A retained RootAccessGroup allows authorised manual actions only on enrolled members, and cannot discover or capture newly appearing siblings without a new explicit scope.
gates.applicability: macOS 13 or later, signed installed companion retaining a root grant across restarts.

evidence.covers: A sibling created later is refused after a restart, which is the no-discovery requirement.
The completed plan narrows to frozen members only while keeping manual member reads.
Members share one persisted root grant until the last owner releases it.

gates.missing_condition: The retained authority is a security-scoped bookmark, and every test substitutes a stub codec encoding the path as Data(url.path.utf8). A path string resolves across restarts unconditionally, so retention of the real grant, which is what this gate qualifies, has never been exercised.
gates.limitations: The frozen-membership logic is well covered and is genuinely independent of the codec. The authority that is supposed to make it enforceable rather than advisory is simulated.

gates.normative_summary: Repeated and external invocations. Hover callbacks, repeated Shortcut and Finder invocations, existing drafts and rapid mixed drops do not overwrite or silently merge unrelated intent.
gates.applicability: macOS 13 or later installed companion across the Shortcuts, Finder and drop routes under repeated invocation.

evidence.covers: Repeated Shortcut runs wait rather than merge.
One drag session is admitted once, so a repeated hover or drop cannot double-admit it.
Confirming one group never submits another, which is the no-silent-merge requirement.
A conflicting replay fails and changes nothing rather than overwriting the original intent.

gates.missing_condition: Section 20.1 requires an installed signed build. Hover callbacks and rapid mixed drops cannot be produced without a real drag source, and repeated Finder invocations need a registered Services entry or Action extension; neither exists.
gates.limitations: The no-merge and no-overwrite invariants are covered on the Shortcuts, group and replay paths. The hover and rapid-drop conditions the gate names specifically are not reproduced.

gates.normative_summary: Keyboard and Shortcuts. Every capture and recovery path is reachable without drag, typed IntentFile expiry is handled, foreground incompatibility is reported, and Shortcut completion never falsely means Added to Core.
gates.applicability: macOS 13 or later installed companion, every capture and recovery path, with drag unavailable.

evidence.covers: The intent owns a copy of every supplied representation before perform returns, which is how IntentFile expiry is handled.
Exactly two review-first intents are offered, so no Shortcut can report an Add.
The opening intent only opens the panel and reads nothing.
An empty or oversize typed selection is refused.

gates.missing_condition: The reachable-without-drag claim spans every capture and recovery path, and there is no accessibility or keyboard test anywhere to establish it. Foreground incompatibility reporting is not asserted, and the Shortcut completion wording is never read by a test. A registered App Intents provider on an installed build is required.
gates.limitations: The two intents' ownership, bounds and review-first behaviour are covered directly. Coverage of the gate's actual subject, keyboard reachability of every path, is zero.

gates.normative_summary: Fresh install and enablement. Actual Services, Quick Actions and Share discovery, the disabled-extension state, system keyboard settings and a Core-only installation all work without Developer Mode or a running Xcode project.
gates.applicability: macOS 13 or later clean host, signed installed companion, no development tooling present.

evidence.covers: The packaged bundle identity is stable and the manifest records the candidate as unsigned and not release eligible.
The packaging refuses to emit a bundle with only one of the two extensions, so an enablement test could not be run against a half-built app.

gates.missing_condition: This gate is the signed-install qualification itself. No codesign, spctl, notarytool or stapler invocation exists in the repository, the packaging manifest declares the candidate qualification_only and unsigned, and nothing registers extensions with pluginkit or reads a disabled-extension state.
gates.limitations: Only the deterministic bundle layout is covered. The README states explicitly that ad-hoc signing is not evidence that macOS has registered App Group-backed extensions, and nothing beyond ad-hoc signing has been attempted.

gates.normative_summary: Coherent update. App, extension and helper version skew, an old running extension, a compatible update, a rollback and a reinstallation all preserve durable work or block explicitly. Source grants are not silently lost or reactivated.
gates.applicability: macOS 13 or later across signed updates and rollbacks of the companion and both extensions.

evidence.covers: A newer schema from a future build is preserved byte for byte rather than rewritten.
An unsupported newer batch schema is preserved rather than discarded, which is the skew case.
A legacy folder ledger gets a default root generation frozen across updates, so grants are not silently reactivated.
Contradictory legacy grant records fail closed rather than picking one.

gates.missing_condition: No signed build exists to update, and no installer owns the update. An old running extension against a new companion requires two signed bundles and macOS extension lifetime behaviour; the grant-preservation half additionally requires real bookmarks, which are stubbed in every test.
gates.limitations: Forward and backward schema compatibility is covered thoroughly at every store. Version skew between actually-running components is not covered, because only one component ever runs.

gates.normative_summary: Platform coexistence. Platform absent, installed, running and closed all use the same native selection owner, grant store, queues and subscriptions.
gates.applicability: macOS 13 or later with Platform in each of its four states alongside Core.

evidence.covers: One companion per installation, which is the shared-owner precondition.
The production environment shares one publication gate across every owner.
The environment owns one observation ledger on the shared gate, so there is one watcher registry.

gates.missing_condition: Platform does not exist in this repository in any form, so none of its four states can be produced. The single-owner invariants are verified within one process only, and the design's requirement of one setting value and one watcher registry across both products has no second participant.
gates.limitations: The companion's internal single-owner structure is covered. Coexistence is, by definition, untestable here.

gates.normative_summary: Office variants. Word, Excel and PowerPoint fixtures plus common compatible-app fixtures for both qualified namespace families, with the same source bytes before and after.
gates.applicability: Every qualified OOXML format on every OS the Core runtime supports. The extractors are platform-agnostic Python.

evidence.covers: Both qualified namespace families decode identically, for the XLSX temporal path.
Both ZIP storage modes an authoring application may emit still read.
A DOCX package is extracted with its comments kept separate from prose.
Three unmodified Microsoft Office Strict-namespace packages (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Open XML SDK revision 431ab05c, MIT) carry only Strict vocabulary namespaces.
Each Strict package extracts successfully and repeatably through the production extractor, and its source bytes keep their pinned SHA-256 before and after.

gates.missing_condition: The Microsoft Office Strict-family slice is closed for Word, Excel and PowerPoint by three upstream Open XML SDK fixtures. The gate also requires Transitional-namespace fixtures from Word, Excel, PowerPoint and common compatible applications, and a before-and-after source-byte comparison across that corpus. Only the Keynote-authored PPTX covers a compatible application, and no Transitional Microsoft Office fixture is committed.
gates.limitations: The Strict fixtures are small upstream test assets, one per format, and were not authored for this repository; the byte comparison is of the fixture file around extraction, not a round trip through an authoring application. Strict and Transitional agreement is still shown only for the XLSX temporal path. No compatible-application Strict fixture exists, so the cross-application matrix this gate asks for is incomplete.

gates.normative_summary: DOCX body and annotations. Nested and merged tables, headers, notes, text boxes, comments, and insert, delete and move revisions, with no conflation of deleted and inserted sentences.
gates.applicability: Every qualified DOCX source on every OS the Core runtime supports.

evidence.covers: Inserted, current and deleted prose are split rather than conflated.
An insertion later deleted stays deleted, and contradictory revision markup is refused.
Nested tables are traversed under an explicit bound.
Text boxes are separate blocks read exactly once.
Notes link by story and id without duplicating their text into prose.
Comment ranges, references and metadata are extracted as annotations.
A section places each of the three header and footer kinds it declares in its own role.
A w:moveTo and a w:moveFrom over a block reach every run they cover, and the moved-in and moved-out text never share a segment.
A move out nested inside a move in stays deleted, and the contradictory nestings are refused rather than resolved.
A merged cell keeps its grid span across a move revision, which is the merged-table case under revision markup.
A rectangular merge carries both spans at one anchor, with its text emitted once.
A nested table keeps its own grid under the cell path that holds it.

gates.limitations: Every condition is asserted against the production DOCX walker, and the no-conflation requirement is covered unusually well: inserted, current, deleted, moved-in and moved-out prose each land in their own segment and role. Fixtures are packages synthesised in memory with zipfile and carry no recorded digest, and no application-authored DOCX exists in this repository.

gates.normative_summary: XLSX formulas. Expression plus stale or missing cache, error values, array and shared formulas and external links, with no calculation and no invented zero.
gates.applicability: Every qualified XLSX source on every OS the Core runtime supports.

evidence.covers: The expression and the saved cache are preserved as distinct values, so nothing is calculated.
Decoding a cache value leaves the expression untouched.
An anomalous cache keeps its number and its freshness marker rather than being replaced.
External links are inert inventory placed after the workbook content, never resolved.
An array formula carries its range, and a shared formula carries its index and range, each as its own kind.
An array or shared formula with no cache records the cache as missing and emits no saved value, so no zero is invented.
A shared master declared after its own follower still resolves, so follower ordering changes nothing.
All seven error spellings are kept as the error the source wrote, with no numeric anomaly and no number substituted for them.
An array formula's cache can itself be an error, and is then not decoded as a number.
A cache that disagrees with its own expression is preserved beside it rather than recomputed, which is the stale-cache case.

gates.limitations: Every value kind the gate enumerates is asserted against the production workbook extractor, and the no-calculation and no-invented-zero invariants are covered on each of them. Staleness is only preserved, never classified: the extractor records cache freshness as unknown, so a cache disagreeing with its expression is kept but is not labelled stale. Fixtures are workbooks synthesised in memory with zipfile and carry no recorded digest.

gates.normative_summary: XLSX sparse and hidden content. Incorrect dimensions, distant sparse cells, hidden rows and sheets and comments, with bounded work and correctly labelled retrieval.
gates.applicability: Every qualified XLSX source on every OS the Core runtime supports.

evidence.covers: Sheet, row and column hidden state is kept on every cell, so hidden content is labelled rather than dropped or silently retrieved.
Comment threads are reported in source order with exact provenance.
Package-level work is bounded by an explicit member count.
Five declared dimensions -- one cell, the whole sheet, an unparsable range, an empty element and none at all -- each read exactly the two cells present.
A dimension declaring A1:Z100 over a single written cell adds no cells and changes no visibility.
A1 and XFD1048576 are both read with their hidden state correct and nothing between them materialised, and a coordinate past the sheet or a malformed column span is refused.
A comment on a visible, hidden or very hidden sheet stays an annotation, with the sheet state carried in the locator rather than suppressing it.
A very hidden sheet stays distinguishable from a hidden one, so retrieval labelling is not collapsed.

gates.limitations: Incorrect dimensions, distant sparse cells, hidden rows, columns and sheets, and comments on each sheet state are all asserted against the production workbook extractor. Bounded work is proven structurally rather than measured: the distant-cell case reads the two corners without materialising the grid between them, and out-of-range coordinates and malformed column spans are refused, but no test counts the work done. Fixtures are workbooks synthesised in memory with no recorded digest.

gates.normative_summary: PPTX. Grouped shapes, notes absent and present, hidden slides, tables, charts, comments and inherited layout text, with no phantom note creation and no duplicated master text.
gates.applicability: Every qualified PPTX source on every OS the Core runtime supports.

evidence.covers: Grouped shape text is reported once at the member that holds it.
The hidden-slide flag rides every segment, so hidden slides are labelled rather than omitted.
Table cells carry their positions and grid dimensions.
An unrelated notes part is ignored, which is the no-phantom-note requirement.
Slide text, tables and related notes are extracted without rendering.
The layout and then the master are reported behind the slide's own text, which is the no-duplicated-master-text requirement.
A chart reports its stored title and every cached point, without recalculating.
A threaded comment carries its whole source claim as an annotation.
The committed receipt binds a Keynote-authored PPTX, production parser source, exact profile, resource peak and successful extracted body, chart, comment and note results.
A chart's embedded Office workbook remains bounded and inert instead of causing a valid presentation to be rejected or recursively opened.
The real-format qualification receipt records fixture, engine and profile digests, resource peaks and exact result hashes.

gates.limitations: The edge-condition fixtures remain deterministic minimal OOXML packages, while the qualification fixture is a real Keynote export containing body text, a table, a chart with an inert embedded workbook, presenter notes and a classic comment. The Keynote comment author was privacy-normalised after export without changing document content.

gates.normative_summary: RTF. Escapes, Unicode and codepages, nested tables, binary groups, notes, revisions and object links, with a bounded parse, stable locators and known exclusions.
gates.applicability: Every qualified RTF source on hosts where the pinned reader build is installed.

evidence.covers: Escapes, Unicode and declared codepages are read by the bounded scanner.
Binary groups are skipped even when their payload holds structural bytes.
Notes, revisions and unknown destinations are inventoried, which is the known-exclusions requirement.
Object links and field risks are named without being resolved or executed.
The parse is bounded by a reachable group-depth limit.
Tables map every cell with stable section, row and column locators.
Locators are stable across repeated extraction.
The committed receipt binds the source DOCX, the ONLYOFFICE-produced RTF, the converter, the pinned reader and the text-only profile by SHA-256.
The ONLYOFFICE-produced RTF carries real nesttableprops, nestrow and itap2 markers.

The production extract_rtf path with an absolute pinned Pandoc 3.12.1 reads that RTF repeatably, with nested cell values, Unicode body text and the receipt's block, segment and inventory counts. Skips only without a host Pandoc 3.12.1.
The canonical extraction result hashes to the value the receipt records.

gates.missing_condition: One application-produced nested-table RTF (ONLYOFFICE Desktop Editors 9.4.0, converted from a generated DOCX) is now read by the pinned Pandoc 3.12.1 and bound by a committed receipt. This external-fixture gate still needs an RTF corpus from further applications, such as Microsoft Word, Apple TextEdit and LibreOffice, and RTF sources exercising notes, revisions and object links as those applications write them.
gates.limitations: The ONLYOFFICE fixture is a single application's conversion of a generated DOCX, not an RTF the application authored from scratch. The pinned reader flattens nested tables into separate AST tables (8 AST tables against 12 nested-table markers in the scanner inventory), so nested structure is evidenced by cell text and counts rather than by a nesting tree. Reader-dependent tests skip on a host without Pandoc 3.12.1; CI installs it. The bounded scanner, inventories, real pinned-reader path and locator stability remain covered directly.

gates.normative_summary: HTML. Malformed markup, tables and spans, hidden and template content, iframe, local-file and network references, with no external access and truthful parser recovery.
gates.applicability: Every qualified HTML and XHTML source on every OS the Core runtime supports.

evidence.covers: Malformed markup recovers and retains its warnings, which is the truthful-recovery requirement.
XHTML refuses where HTML recovers, so recovery is reported per profile rather than assumed.
A spanning cell claims every column it covers.
A rowspan holds its column against the rows below.
Hidden content is published in its own role rather than mixed into prose.
No non-body role reaches the default retrieval roles.
Link and image targets, local or remote, are inventoried without resolution.
No reference causes an external action.
The admission parse also takes no external action, so the earlier parse is covered too.
A template's text, its nested markup and its script land in the hidden role rather than in prose, and its image and link stay unresolved references.
A template nested inside another non-body element neither leaks into prose nor is counted twice.
An iframe is inventoried under its own kind with its scheme and target unresolved, with open, socket and subprocess patched to raise, and a srcdoc iframe yields no reference at all.
An iframe's fallback markup is published as hidden content, so it contributes no body prose.

gates.limitations: Malformed recovery, spans, hidden and template roles, the iframe kind and the no-external-access rule are all asserted against the production extractor, the last by patching open, socket and subprocess to raise. The iframe inventory holds on any CPython 3.11, but the assertion that an iframe carries no prose of its own depends on the interpreter shipping iframe in HTMLParser.CDATA_CONTENT_ELEMENTS, which 3.11.15 does and earlier 3.11 patch releases do not; CI pins only the 3.11 minor. Fixtures are markup written inline with no recorded digest.

gates.normative_summary: Delimited text. Quoted newlines, escaped delimiters, BOM and UTF-16, duplicate headers, ragged rows, formula-like strings and leading zeroes, with exact fields and locators.
gates.applicability: Every qualified CSV and TSV source on every OS the Core runtime supports.

evidence.covers: Quoted newlines, empty fields and formula-like strings are preserved.
A declared encoding reads the same fields and consumes the byte-order mark.
Ragged rows keep their own field counts and are warned about.
Field text is carried through verbatim, which preserves leading zeroes.
Locators name the record, the column and the physical lines.
Formula-like strings stay values and nothing is evaluated.
An undeclared or malformed encoding is refused rather than guessed.
For CSV and TSV alike, a delimiter escaped by quoting and a quote escaped by doubling both yield the exact field, with a backslash left as an ordinary character.
A BOM-declared UTF-16 LE or BE source reads the same fields and the same locators as its UTF-8 twin, with the encoding recorded as the declared codec.
Repeated and empty labels in the first record keep their source text and their ordinals, recorded as preserved_as_record rather than interpreted as headers.

gates.limitations: UTF-16 is accepted when declared by its byte-order mark; BOM-less UTF-16 is deliberately refused rather than guessed. The reader has no header mode, so repeated labels in the first record are preserved verbatim as data with distinct ordinals rather than collapsed into a mapping. Fixtures are byte literals rather than separately hashed files.

gates.normative_summary: Raster formats. JPEG, PNG and static WebP, multipage TIFF, HEIF primary and auxiliary frames, EXIF orientations and HEIF rotation, with no double rotation and no omitted primary frame.
gates.applicability: Every qualified raster format on hosts where the pinned decoders, including pillow-heif, are installed.

evidence.covers: Multipage TIFF frames are units and reduced subfiles are excluded.
HEIF primary frames are distinct units with a recorded default, so none is omitted.
HEIF rotation is not applied twice.
EXIF orientation is applied once and the transform is recorded.
Static WebP is accepted while an animated one is refused.
A declared media type must agree with the detected container, so a format cannot be mislabelled into another's path.
The committed receipt binds a macOS Image I/O-authored HEIC, the exact Pillow, pillow-heif and libheif decoder build, extraction profile, resource peak and successful primary-frame result.
The real-format qualification receipt records fixture, decoder and profile digests, resource peaks and exact result hashes.

gates.limitations: The frame, orientation and animation edge cases remain generated deterministically in tests. They are complemented by a committed HEIC encoded by macOS Image I/O and a receipt binding its exact bytes to the production Pillow, pillow-heif and libheif decoder build. A broader camera-vendor metadata corpus would increase compatibility confidence but is not a condition named by this gate.

gates.normative_summary: PDF mixed page. A native heading plus a scanned body, both searchable once with correct spatial source mapping. Reliable embedded text remains searchable when OCR returns no accepted words.
gates.applicability: Every qualified PDF on hosts where the pinned OCR engine and its language models are installed.

evidence.covers: The scanned region below a native header is retained alongside it.
Where both methods agree the result is one segment with two observations, which is the searchable-once requirement.
Both methods map into one geometry space, which is the spatial source mapping.
Reliable embedded text stays searchable when OCR accepts no words.
The committed macOS qualification receipt binds the ten-page mixed native-and-scanned PDF, extraction profile, Tesseract 5.5.3 binary, eng and osd model resources, and successful result digests.
The real-engine qualification receipt records exact fixture, engine, language-model, profile and result hashes for the mixed-page PDF run.

gates.limitations: The focused mixed-page behavior tests use an injected recognition engine so that geometry, deduplication and empty-OCR cases remain deterministic. They are complemented by a committed macOS receipt from the production extractor with Tesseract 5.5.3 and pinned eng and osd model hashes over a ten-page mixed native-and-scanned fixture.

gates.normative_summary: PDF OCR conflicts. Native and OCR text disagree, an invisible prior OCR layer is present, and a repeated footer appears at distinct positions. Alternatives are preserved without sentence duplication.
gates.applicability: Every qualified PDF on hosts where the pinned OCR engine and its language models are installed.

evidence.covers: Material disagreement becomes a linked alternative rather than concatenated text.
A repeated footer at distinct positions is never deduplicated away.
Output identity separates method, language and confidence, which is how alternatives stay distinguishable.

A hand-built page whose text is rendering mode 3 over a full-page raster paints identically to the raster alone and differently when the same text is visible; the layer is decoded as native text with page, geometry space, rotation, crop box and distinct per-line boxes.
An OCR reading that agrees with the invisible layer is stored once, with both methods recorded.
A conflicting reading is kept as a hidden alternative linked to the layer line, and neither amount is appended to the other.
A footer repeated at three positions in the invisible layer stays three segments, each paired with the reading over its own region.

gates.limitations: The recognition engine is injected throughout, which is the right instrument for a gate about how disagreement and position are handled, but it means no pinned engine build or language-model digest is recorded with the result. The invisible-layer PDF is hand-built in-test with no recorded fixture hash, and the three conditions are exercised in separate tests rather than on one page.

gates.normative_summary: OCR confidence. Empty, zero or sentinel, below-threshold and mixed-confidence output. Empty OCR is distinct from the combined page result, with no false blank and no success claim.
gates.applicability: Every qualified image and PDF raster unit on every OS the Core runtime supports. The confidence contract is decided by the extractor, not by the engine.

evidence.covers: An empty pass records no reliable OCR text rather than a blank success.
Zero, negative and sentinel confidence values never become certainty.
Below-threshold candidates stay observations outside search.
Mixed-confidence output is flagged by both median and share.
A source with no useful text is not reported as a plain success.
An empty OCR pass is distinct from the combined page result, which still carries the embedded text.

gates.limitations: The recognition engine is injected, which is the correct instrument for this gate because the subject is how the extractor treats confidence values rather than how well recognition performs, but it means no pinned engine build or resource digest is recorded with the result as section 11.15 requires. Images are synthesised with PIL and no fixture hash is recorded. The thresholds exercised are the build's own packaged constants.

gates.normative_summary: OCR language. English works offline, two and three explicit languages are honoured, and an absent model refuses the OCR unit without auto-download and without silent language substitution.
gates.applicability: Every qualified image and PDF raster unit, on hosts where the managed language resources have been installed.

evidence.covers: The measurement itself: on arm64 macOS 27.0.0, an assembled candidate whose 23 packaged resources were digest-verified recognised a generated English image and read an RTF through the confined worker, with both engines run from an environment holding nothing but the operating system's own PATH.

The lane that produced it, and the eight gates it holds a run to -- assembly, bundle coherence, payload verification, relocation, an offline engine start, offline English recognition, an offline RTF read and the refusal of a tampered packaged byte. Every gate starts closed.
The committed record is re-verified offline on every repository run, so an edited record or a grown gate set fails rather than standing.
The production resolution: English and the orientation data come from the verified packaged bytes, with an absolute packaged engine and model directory, and every resolved path is inside the payload.
A manifest that does not decode, a packaged byte that moved and a packaged file that is gone each resolve to no payload at all, so no engine is invoked and no model hash is claimed.
An absent model is a needs-language report, never a silent English fallback.
Two and three explicit languages keep their configured order.
A language the host happens to have is never discovered, so there is no implicit acquisition.
A model whose bytes do not match its pinned digest is never invoked.
There is no bare-name or search-path route to the engine: resources naming no absolute packaged executable are refused before any process starts.
The service executor settles a missing language as needs-ocr-language rather than a failure or a success.

gates.missing_condition: English now works offline, and the run is recorded rather than asserted: the committed record above was produced on this project's macOS host from an assembled candidate whose packaged Pandoc, Tesseract, relocated library closure and bundled English and orientation models were digest-verified first, and the recognition went through the production path -- the installation authority, the frozen resource identities and the confined worker -- not a harness around it. What the repository cannot do is make that measurement again. Pandoc and the Tesseract models are not redistributed here, so neither CI nor scripts/preflight has engine bytes to assemble a candidate from, and the lane refuses to run anywhere but macOS. The repository therefore re-verifies the record offline on every run and proves the packaging, verification, relocation, refusal and runtime-binding contracts with synthetic payloads, which is everything except repeating the recognition itself.
gates.limitations: The measurement is one host, one architecture and one engine build: arm64 macOS 27.0.0 with pandoc 3.12.1 and tesseract 5.5.3, whose source digests the record pins. Nothing has run on Intel. The resource manifest is not *signed*, which 11.12.2 asks for: the digests sit in plain JSON beside the payload, which catches a substituted file but not an attacker who rewrites both, and closing it needs the release owner WP-00 row 13 leaves unbound. The candidate is qualification-only, unsigned beyond the ad-hoc seal that makes a relocated Mach-O runnable on Apple silicon. A selection mixing a bundled language with a managed one is served by the managed cache alone, because one Tesseract invocation takes one model directory, so it reports English missing until that is installed through the managed route. The bundled models consume no managed-cache capacity and no second pool was introduced for them.

gates.normative_summary: Embedded document image profile. Off reports an exact inventory, on OCRs qualified admitted Office, RTF and HTML raster bytes, and linked remote images never load.
gates.applicability: Every qualified Office, RTF and HTML source carrying embedded or linked raster bytes.

evidence.covers: With the profile off the result reports what it excluded rather than omitting it silently.
Linked remote images are inventoried without being loaded.
External package relationships, including linked images, are inventoried without resolution.
A DOCX embedded raster is decoded, handed to the resolved recognition catalogue at its own pixel size, and its reading anchored to the image part showing it.
An XLSX embedded raster is recognised on the same seam and anchored to the picture showing it.
A PPTX embedded raster is recognised on the same seam and anchored to the picture showing it.
An RTF picture payload is recognised and anchored to the control group holding it.
An inline HTML data payload is recognised and anchored to the element showing it.
With the profile off the payload is never decoded and the outcome names the exclusion, which is the exact-inventory half.
Through extract_document with a real local engine, a DOCX embedded raster's own words are recovered only when the settings say to examine it.
The same holds for an RTF embedded raster through extract_document with a real local engine.
The same holds for an HTML inline raster, and its file-scheme reference stays unresolved.

gates.limitations: The profile-on half runs for all five container formats -- DOCX, XLSX, PPTX, RTF and HTML -- but the unconditional evidence injects a recording engine over digest-pinned stand-in model bytes, so it proves the extracted raster reaches a resolved catalogue at the right size and that the reading is anchored to the right part, not that pixels were read correctly. The cases that recover an embedded image's own words through a real engine exist for every one of the five formats, but their fixture skips wherever no tesseract with the English and orientation models is installed, which includes both CI workflows and scripts/preflight. The HTML unconditional case calls the module-private HTML extractor rather than extract_document. Every raster is drawn with PIL and every package built in memory, with no recorded fixture digest.

gates.normative_summary: Resource adversaries. ZIP bomb, duplicate paths, DTD and entity declarations, huge dimensions, excessive frames, parser timeout and output overflow, with no native or Core cap breach.
gates.applicability: Every qualified format on every OS the Core runtime supports. The bounds are the packaged constants of this build.

evidence.covers: A compression bomb is rejected at the shipped limits.
Duplicate and otherwise ambiguous member paths are rejected.
DTD and entity declarations are rejected before parsing.
The aggregate bound is enforced from the stream rather than from the declared directory, so a lying header cannot breach the cap.
A huge declared dimension is refused from the header before allocation.
Excessive frames are a truthful refusal.
A parser timeout yields an explicit unknown rather than a proven blank.
Output overflow stays partial rather than being reported complete.
The markup depth, node and source bounds still refuse once the admission parse is in the path.

gates.limitations: Every adversary is synthesised in-test, which is appropriate here, but the bounds asserted are this build's own packaged constants rather than values a separate native or Core cap supplied, so no-cap-breach is proven against the extractor's own limits and not against an enclosing process or supervisor budget. Peak memory and CPU are not measured, so the refusals are shown to happen without showing what resources were consumed before them. Section 11.15's resource-peak record does not exist.

gates.normative_summary: Worker isolation. Attempted file and network reads from document fields or from dependencies reach nothing: only admitted input, packaged models and private scratch are accessible.
gates.applicability: Every qualified format processed by the document worker on every OS the Core runtime supports.

evidence.covers: Removing the attempt directory touches nothing outside it. A child that left work/escape pointing at a directory of the host's had that directory remoded from 0755 to 0700 by the cleanup, because os.walk lists a symlinked directory among its directory names and chmod by name follows it. Modes are now restored only through descriptors opened with O_NOFOLLOW, and this asserts the link targets' mode and content are unchanged while the scratch is gone. test_cleanup_follows_no_link_standing_where_the_scratch_root_is asserts the same for a link standing where the attempt directory itself should be.

Cleanup is bounded and truthful. A removal that fails leaves a copy of the admitted source on the host, and that is reported as worker_scratch_not_removed rather than returned as a successful extraction. test_a_cleanup_failure_never_replaces_the_cause_the_worker_already_had shows a worker that already failed keeps its own typed cause, and test_the_cleanup_walk_is_bounded_and_says_so_rather_than_running_on shows the walk stops at an entry ceiling and reports a residue rather than running on over whatever a parser created.

The reply is read only from a regular file. A FIFO left at the reply's name would hold the parent open indefinitely, after the wall-clock budget that bounded the attempt had already been settled; the open refuses to block and to follow a link, and the descriptor is fstat-ed before a byte is read. This asserts a bounded typed refusal rather than a wait; test_a_reply_that_is_a_directory_is_not_read_as_one and the device case cover the other objects a parser can leave at that name.

The reply protocol is exact. Every status carries exactly the fields it is answered with -- an outcome where there is one, a detail where there is a reason, nothing else -- so a reply that is merely near enough for its status is refused instead of partially read. test_no_statement_about_the_document_is_read_from_an_unsealed_child adds that each of the three replies which say something about the source is refused unless the child names the seal.

The frozen settings crossing into the child are an exact key set, so a header carrying an extra or a missing field is refused rather than read for the parts of it that look familiar. test_pinned_ocr_resources_carrying_an_unknown_field_are_refused holds the pinned OCR resources, the verified model directory among them, to the same exactness.

The child's executable search path is a module constant and not the service's PATH, so whoever can set one variable on the service cannot choose which binary a parser runs. It no longer names a locally administered prefix at all: the pinned Pandoc and the OCR engine are absolute paths out of the verified installation payload, so the lookup those directories existed for is gone and nothing under /opt or /usr/local is readable to a sealed child.

A real child process sealed by the macOS adapter is refused a stream and a datagram socket and refused every read, write and stat outside the admitted source, the packaged code, the pinned models, the verified packaged runtime root and its private scratch, while reads, writes and an execution inside that scope still succeed. The same process attempts the same things before sealing itself and is allowed them, so the refusals are read as the seal and not as the host, and the package-manager prefixes it could list before are refused after.

Asked to seal a process on a platform this build has no adapter for, the adapter raises rather than returning an unconfined process, so there is no code path on which a caller reads a hostile document unsealed.

The parent's half of failing closed: a reply that reports a real outcome while naming no confinement is refused at the protocol boundary, so a worker built or patched to skip the seal cannot deliver an extraction.

In the production capture-outbox pass, a worker that could not be sealed, outran its budget, crashed or was stopped by a resource ceiling settles the obligation as failed under that typed reason, never as source_invalid, with nothing projected and the retained immutable source intact for a later retry.
The same mapping through the reprocess handler and the governed dispatcher: the stored result carries the worker's typed reason, nothing is published, and the retained bytes are unchanged.

The reply is created exclusively and opened without following a link at both ends, so a parser that held write access to the scratch while the document was being read cannot aim either the write or the read at anything else on the host.
The admitted bytes still extract: a confined child returns the same outcome, segments and output digest the in-process adapters produce, for plain text, Markdown, delimited text and markup.
Both production call sites, the capture outbox and the reprocess handler, resolve their extraction seam to the confined child rather than the in-process adapters.
A seal that cannot be established returns a typed isolation refusal with no outcome at all, so the worker never falls back to an unconfined or in-process run.

A child stopped by the CPU ceiling's own signal is reported as a resource-limit outcome rather than as a crash or as a verdict on the source. test_a_worker_that_outruns_its_budget_is_a_timeout adds that a child outrunning its wall-clock budget has its session killed and is reported as a timeout. Both are per-attempt reasons distinct from the aggregate memory and CPU reasons the supervisor raises.

The 1 GiB resident ceiling of 17.1 and the cumulative budget of 11.13 are enforced over the job's whole session group rather than per process: four processes, each inside a ceiling derived from measuring them individually, breach it together. test_cumulative_cpu_outlives_every_descendant_that_exits_and_restarts charges descendants that were started, spent their CPU and were reaped between two samples, so a restart cannot reset the budget, and test_a_resource_breach_kills_the_tree_reaps_the_child_and_says_which drives one breach end to end through the production route.

A job is finished only once its tree is. The root's exit is read from its own accounting while it is still a zombie, never by reaping it: test_a_root_that_burns_and_exits_between_ticks_is_over_budget charges a root that spent its budget and exited between samples, and this test kills a group still holding a descendant before the leader is reaped rather than returning the reply it outlived. test_no_source_byte_is_offered_before_one_real_sample_has_succeeded holds the other end, and test_an_exit_race_mid_pass_cannot_produce_an_accepted_undercounted_sample discards a pass a member vanished from.
A reply whose transported segments do not re-hash to the output digest it reports is refused, so the boundary cannot change what was extracted.
The child's whole environment is built by the parent from a fixed set of seven variables, so no credential, workspace path or other inherited configuration travels with it.
The worker names only the resource limits the host actually binds, so RLIMIT_AS is absent on macOS rather than claimed and unenforced.

The engine invocation is built only from trusted resources, so a document field cannot reach the command line, and test_a_verified_model_manifest_is_the_only_language_source adds that only a verified manifest supplies models, so packaged resources are the sole model source.

The external reader's arguments stay fixed and carry no path from the document, and argument zero is the absolute packaged executable the frozen settings named rather than a bare word resolved against a search path.
A relationship target outside the package is rejected.

gates.missing_condition: The boundary exists and is enforced on macOS only. Production extraction runs in a child whose whole environment is seven fixed variables, under a bounded versioned JSON protocol, and the parent accounts that child's whole session group against the 1 GiB resident ceiling of 17.1 and one cumulative CPU budget per job. On macOS the child seals itself with a deny-by-default seatbelt profile before reading a source byte, and a real child-process test proves the seal denies the network and every read, write and stat outside the admitted source, the packaged code, the models, the packaged runtime root and the private scratch. The packaged-engine scope is now closed: 11.2's Pandoc and Tesseract, their relocated library closure and the bundled models are staged into the candidate, digest-pinned in the manifest and reached by absolute path, so the child's search path names no package-manager prefix. What remains is the platform: Linux and Windows have neither adapter and fail closed under worker_supervision_unavailable, so nothing is processed there -- a product gap, not evidence -- while the applicability above is every OS Core supports.
gates.limitations: Containment is proven by a probe inside the sealed process making the reads, stats, executions and connections itself, unsealed then sealed, so refusals are anchored against this host's unconfined behaviour. That is the worker's own authority, which a hostile parser holds too, but that path is not driven to one. mach-lookup stays open: dyld needs it and no bounded service list is qualified; the network denial closes what a looked-up service could offer. file-read-metadata is granted on the ancestors of in-scope paths, which macOS needs to resolve the /var symlink every scratch sits behind. The packaged payload is unsigned beyond an ad-hoc seal, which is what makes a relocated Mach-O runnable on Apple silicon and is not a release identity. Resident size is sampled every tenth of a second, which is the resolution of that ceiling and not a kernel-hard cap, and shared pages count once per mapping process, erring towards refusal. Cumulative CPU is charged in full for any descendant reaped inside the group, but one orphaned to launchd takes its unsampled tail with it.

gates.normative_summary: Reprocess races. Two reprocess jobs complete in reverse order, with delayed admission, a changed or null base, source removal after admission immediately before promotion, and a newer source capture. No stale head promotion and no resurrection.
gates.applicability: The Core canonical extraction and head-ordering boundary on every OS the runtime supports.

evidence.covers: Two jobs completing in reverse order leave the newer head standing.
Source removal after admission and immediately before promotion fences the result.
The source and extraction heads cannot move together, so a newer source capture cannot drag the extraction head with it.
An explicit null base is handled as its own case rather than as a missing value.
A reprocess against a stale expected head is historical, never promoted.
A changed base or profile is an idempotency conflict and no extraction runs, which is the no-resurrection rule.

gates.limitations: Core side only, in a single process against the real SQLite store and ServiceRunner. The jobs are sequenced deterministically by each test rather than genuinely raced across workers, so the ordering invariants are proven over commit sequence and not under concurrent contention. Delayed admission is injected by ordering the calls rather than by a real worker being slow.

gates.normative_summary: Retrieval publication. A previous authorised result stays available until a verified replacement, and a failed extraction does not destroy it. Evidence deletion, expiry or suppression, or retrieval-authority loss after admission, defeats late publication through the atomic eligibility guard.
gates.applicability: The Core retrieval publication boundary on every OS the runtime supports.

evidence.covers: A failed extraction settles without publishing and destroys nothing.
A verified replacement is what publishes a new projection.
Evidence deletion after admission defeats late publication through the eligibility guard.
Expiry does not fall back to an earlier result.
A removed source refuses extractions while keeping its existing heads available.
Suppression survives: a removed capture is never promoted.

gates.limitations: Core side only, single process, real SQLite store. Retrieval-authority loss is exercised as retention expiry and source removal rather than as a revoked credential or a lost authorisation, because there is no authentication boundary in these tests. The late publication is ordered by the test rather than arriving concurrently, so the guard is proven atomic over a commit sequence rather than under genuine contention.

gates.normative_summary: Governance. Documents containing prompts, executable instructions or business claims create evidence and derived records only, without workflow execution and without knowledge approval.
gates.applicability: The Core governed-knowledge boundary for evidence captured from any document source.

evidence.covers: A captured document whose whole body is a model-directed instruction, an executable-looking formula and a business claim is derived to evidence and one proposed candidate by capture_document_bytes followed by process_capture_outbox alone, while every workflow, provider, runtime-run, effect, chat-turn and tool-call table stays empty.
That same body arrives in the derived content as one JSON string, byte for byte, with nothing resolved, expanded or evaluated.

The derivation's whole first-party runtime import closure, resolved statically by file and excluding type-checking-only imports, contains no workflow, provider, chat, agent, tool, decision-runtime, execution or MCP module, so no document content can reach one.

The lineage records the extraction as deterministic, which is the one variant migration 0009 forbids a model, an inference configuration, a prompt template and a randomness seed, and all six of those columns are asserted null.
No approval or admission appears: the record is visible only as a candidate, and no governed assembly, supersession, approval or governance transition exists.
Executable-looking content stays a value in the extractor that produced the segment.
A script body and an event handler are inert text in the extractor that produced the segment.

gates.limitations: Driven by the production trigger: the hostile document is captured and processed, and the derivation the capture-outbox pass performs is what the inert-content and no-approval assertions are made over, so no listed evidence invokes the derivation seam to make the gate hold. The document is plain text, which the extractor renders as one segment, so the junction is proved once per capture rather than across many segments; the per-format inert-content half is proved separately by the delimited and HTML extractor tests cited above. No workflow engine participates in any of it, asserted two ways -- the tables are empty afterwards, and the modules that could run one are not in the derivation's import closure at all -- but the second claim is scoped to omnivia_core_runtime and to the derivation module: omnivia_core.contracts.v1 is reached for canonical JSON and carries workflow *schemas*, which validate wire shapes and start nothing, and document_processing, which now calls the derivation, is the capture-outbox pass and is not itself closure-checked. Execution is on the single ubuntu-latest Core acceptance host.

gates.normative_summary: Create an individual watch. Explicit consent, a frozen caller, workspace and generation, and an ordinary later edit publishes without another approval.
gates.applicability: macOS 13 or later companion watching a single file on a local volume.

evidence.covers: The watch waits for canonical admission of the consent, then a later edit queues against the current head with no further approval.
An automatic capture requires a matching binding and standing consent, so consent is explicit and bound.
The consent and configuration generations must match the persisted watch, which is the frozen generation.
The frozen caller and workspace binding must match at publication.
Nothing is read or queued before the baseline is admitted, so consent precedes observation.

gates.limitations: Unsigned swift test process on the macos-latest runner with OS and Xcode versions unrecorded. The clock is injected, the delivery client is a fake, and the edit is a direct file write rather than an FSEvents signal, so Core admission and real event delivery are both simulated. Section 21.12 additionally requires signed installed access and real retrieval, neither of which this run provides.

gates.normative_summary: Folder once, with recursion on and off. The preview and the actual membership agree, and an unapproved descendant is never read when recursion is off.
gates.applicability: macOS 13 or later companion one-off folder intake on a local volume, both recursion settings.

evidence.covers: The reviewed preview and the actual scope agree on membership.
With recursion off an unapproved descendant is never read.
With recursion off a subfolder is not even listed, so nothing unapproved is enumerated either.
With recursion on, depth beyond the reviewed limit is excluded rather than silently traversed.

gates.limitations: Unsigned swift test process on the macos-latest runner, OS and Xcode versions unrecorded. Trees are real temporary directories, which makes the traversal evidence genuine, but the root grant is a stub bookmark codec encoding the path as Data(url.path.utf8), so the authority behind the refusal is simulated. Section 21.12's signed installed access is not provided.

gates.normative_summary: New files appear during a one-off plan. Frozen membership excludes new entries, and there is no silent expansion after restart.
gates.applicability: macOS 13 or later companion one-off folder plan across a restart.

evidence.covers: Membership is frozen at approval and a sibling created later is refused after a restart.
The frozen manifest cannot be widened or rebound.
A restart continues the same frozen manifest rather than rebuilding it.

gates.limitations: Unsigned swift test process on the macos-latest runner, OS and Xcode versions unrecorded. The restart is a store reopen rather than a process relaunch, and the root grant is a stub bookmark codec, though frozen membership is a manifest property that does not depend on the codec.
