evidence.covers: An unusual disappearance requires review before members are marked absent.
A partial scan does not touch the prior inventory, so it cannot cause a false deletion.
An unavailable provider must report that nothing was covered, so a remount failure is not absence.
An unlistable root is not reported as an empty folder.

Twenty absences below a tenth are ordinary; 28 of 280 present reaches review though it is under a tenth of the 300 ever enrolled, so the share is of the present inventory; fifteen of 150 is exactly a tenth and one item short of twenty, so also ordinary.
Thirty of 101 members gone, past both thresholds, with an unreadable subtree then with the root moved away: both end needsAccess, nothing is marked absent, no review is raised and nothing is queued.

gates.limitations: Executed and passing on 2026-10-16 as unsigned swift test cases under a controllable clock, over temporary folders and the production DocumentIntakeEnvironment, queue and subscription store. Remount failure is simulated by moving the watched folder away, not by unmounting a volume. Coverage is enforced by the scan throwing before the thresholds are reached, so the partial-scan test is the only evidence of that precondition at this layer.

gates.normative_summary: Scan and recursion limits. An incomplete scope is visible, and there is no arbitrary-prefix ingestion and no mass absence inference.
gates.applicability: macOS 13 or later companion scope policy and reconciliation executor on every watched root.

evidence.covers: A subtree that fails partway leaves the scan visibly incomplete.
Incomplete coverage is reported to the person as counts, so it is visible without disclosing paths.
Containment is component bounded, which is exactly the no-arbitrary-prefix requirement.
A scan reaching its bound is reported as not finished.
The examined-entry bound is likewise reported as an unfinished pass.
A partial scan touches no inventory, which is the no-mass-absence-inference requirement.
Depth beyond the reviewed recursion limit is excluded.

gates.limitations: Unsigned swift test process on the macos-latest runner, OS and Xcode versions unrecorded. Bounds are exercised against reduced test limits over small temporary trees rather than at the shipped limits over a large real tree, so the reporting is proven while the limit values themselves are only pinned as the reviewed design bounds in a separate test.

gates.normative_summary: An unusual review, then more changes. The approval is bound to the reviewed inventory and configuration, and a materially changed review scope is updated.
gates.applicability: macOS 13 or later companion after an unusual-change review, when further changes arrive.

evidence.covers: A rejected folder update requires review and can be retried, which is the review binding.
An acknowledgement is scoped to the same subscription, configuration and epoch it was made for.
A configuration generation that moved on is stale, so an approval cannot outlive its configuration.

The approval is recorded against the reviewed inventory's signature. A reviewed member arriving at a different size is a materially changed scope: it is refreshed and reviewed again, nothing is published, the outrun approval is cleared, and approving the new screen drains exactly that.
The signature differs by subscription, configuration generation, consent generation, a changed member's size, and a member shown as missing; the same inventory signs identically.

gates.limitations: Executed and passing on 2026-10-16 as unsigned swift test cases under a controllable clock, over temporary folders and the production DocumentIntakeEnvironment, queue and subscription store. This build has no path that reconfigures a subscription or re-grants consent, so the configuration and consent half of the binding is proven as a difference in the signature the production scan compares, not by reconfiguring a live watch.

gates.normative_summary: Signed update, downgrade and uninstall. A stable grant owner, a preserved queue and subscription schema and no duplicate watcher, with unknown schemas preserved and original files untouched.
gates.applicability: macOS 13 or later across a signed update, a rollback and an uninstall of the companion.

evidence.covers: The grant owner stays stable across an update rather than being re-derived.
An unknown newer schema is preserved exactly rather than rewritten.
One observation ledger per environment, which is the no-duplicate-watcher rule.
Original bytes and attributes are unchanged by the companion's own reads.

gates.missing_condition: No signed build exists to update, roll back or uninstall, and no installer owns those operations. Grant-owner stability across a reinstall additionally depends on real security-scoped bookmarks, which every test stubs to a path string.
gates.limitations: Schema preservation and the single-watcher invariant are covered thoroughly within one process. The three lifecycle events the gate names are each simulated by writing a document with a different version number or by reopening a store.

gates.normative_summary: Add with Keep updated while the initial association or activation is interrupted. The initial capture and the pending subscription retain their identities, no background reads occur before confirmed canonical activation, and there is no late reactivation after a local stop.
gates.applicability: macOS 13 or later companion establishing a watch alongside a first capture, across an interruption.

evidence.covers: An interruption right after the intent and root write orphans nothing and recovers in full, so identities are retained.
An interruption before activation holds both owners without granting discovery, which is the no-background-reads requirement.
An interruption after activation retires the intent without repeating the work.
Nothing is read or queued before the baseline is canonically admitted.
A pending establishment is finished before a new submission counts watches, so a partial state is not double-counted.

A Keep updated folder add still waiting for Core survives a restart with the same subscription, root, members and baseline items; nothing is observed or queued, and not even a file that appears meanwhile is looked at, until Core confirms the baselines, which activates that same watch.

A folder watch stopped while its baseline awaits Core stays stopped when the admission lands late, records no capture against itself, queues nothing, and does not resume, in the same process and after a restart.
A late refusal of the baseline does not send a stopped folder watch to review, which Resume accepts.

A Keep updated file add still waiting for Core survives a restart as the same subscription, access reference and baseline item; the source is never read again and nothing is observed, even after a change signal, until Core's admission is confirmed, which activates that same subscription.

A file watch stopped while its first capture awaits Core stays stopped whether the answer is an admission or a refusal: no capture is recorded against it, it is not paused (which Resume accepts), it is not observed, and it does not resume, in the same process and after a restart.

gates.limitations: Executed and passing on 2026-10-16 as unsigned swift test cases over temporary folders and the production DocumentIntakeEnvironment, queue and subscription stores, for both the folder and the individual-file path. The interruptions are store-level and a restart is a second environment over the same state rather than a real process kill; Core admission and refusal are applied to the queue directly, and the bookmark codec is stubbed. A file add registers its watch in the same critical section as the queue commit rather than behind a durable pending intent, so a kill between those two writes would leave the capture queued without a watch; the add reports that case as queued once only rather than hiding it, and it is not modelled here. The late-receipt guard is in FileMonitoringCoordinator and FolderMonitoringCoordinator; stopping is final for either, and re-adding is the only route back.

gates.normative_summary: A profile or language resource update during queued or active work. The pending input, profile and resource digest are unchanged, and exact worker resources are retained or the operation pauses, never substituted beneath its key. A full 512 MiB managed cache evicts only unpinned resources or defers installation and new-profile admission; pinned resources and the cap remain intact.
gates.applicability: The Core document worker and its managed OCR resource store on every OS the runtime supports.

evidence.covers: The capacity constant the gate names is pinned at exactly 512 MiB.
A resource whose bytes do not match its digest is never invoked, so nothing is substituted beneath its key.
A text-only profile pins nothing, which bounds what the pin set means.
An install into a full cache evicts another language's unpinned resource to fit, names what it evicted and deletes its directory.
Across every install order, the victims are the shortest prefix of the cache's own stable-key order that covers the shortfall.
A leased resource is never a victim either, so a running extraction cannot lose its bytes to an install.
A resource whose bytes fail verification is neither evicted nor counted as reclaimable room.
When eviction cannot free enough, the installation is deferred with the capacity it needed, the pins stay held and the accounted bytes stay at or under the cap.
Two concurrent processes racing for the same room cannot both spend it: the one eviction cannot absorb defers, and the pinned entry and the cap both survive.
A newer model revision installed while a capture is queued never reaches it: the frozen profile keeps the admitted model hashes and its digest is unchanged.
A language-preference change and a model change together leave the queued capture's admitted profile digest alone.
A queued capture whose pin was lost pauses rather than re-pinning, which is the pauses-rather-than-substitutes half.
During active work the resolved selection is held: a removal attempted mid-extraction is refused as pinned and reconciliation changes nothing.

A profile rewrite and a model-revision install together, across a real restart, leave the queued capture's retained bytes, source digest, source length, frozen preferences, frozen resource identities, admitted profile digest and operation key at the admitted values, and the extraction is admitted under the key derived from that digest.

A new profile needing an uninstalled language the owner's verified catalogue declares, against a cache accounted to the full 512 MiB with every byte-bearing set pinned, is deferred as language_storage_full with the declared required bytes, the zero available bytes and the exact requested identity -- not refused as missing: no capture row, no pin, the cap, the pins and the queued obligation intact, an install of that language refused against the same real admission pin, and the identical admission accepted once that obligation settles.

A capture admitted wholly against the bundled models whose packaged bytes are then replaced pauses rather than settling under a resource condition, and the restored payload settles the same row under the admitted digest.
The same pause when the verified payload is gone entirely, so an unrecoverable exact bundled resource never silently takes a different terminal path.

The admission-time reservation compares the requested sets' summed declared size against the free remainder plus what it verifies as reclaimable, so 300 reclaimable bytes beside 100 free ones does not accommodate a 500-byte requirement; the deferral states both figures and the exact sets, and evicts nothing.

A three-language selection's requirement is the sum of the sets this cache has not installed: the already-installed member costs nothing and is not counted as room for its siblings either, and the figure named is that sum alone.

A cache accounted to the real 512 MiB whose byte-bearing set is pinned reserves nothing, refuses with language_storage_full, zero available bytes and the exact requested identity, and leaves the state document byte-for-byte unchanged.

Through production admission: a cache at its cap with a small unpinned verified set defers a profile whose declared language costs a megabyte, naming the declared requirement and the reclaimable bytes, evicting nothing; and the same cache admits the same profile as a missing language once the requirement is one those bytes cover.

A selection the verified catalogue does not declare, in whole or in part, establishes no capacity requirement and is recorded as the missing-language condition rather than deferred on an invented size.

Through the production dispatcher: the deferral reaches a caller as its own retryable error carrying typed required_bytes, available_bytes, requested_languages and requested resource identities in ApiError.details, surviving the contract encoding, with no capture row or outbox row written.

The installation half of the same reservation through the owner-local administrative CLI: a full cache refuses the install with language_storage_full and the required and available byte figures as fields of the result document.

gates.missing_condition: One condition remains, and it is the trusted source rather than the mechanism. Deferring a new-profile admission for capacity needs the declared byte_size of the managed resource sets the profile names and this cache has not got, and the only authority this build accepts for one is a model manifest verified by distribution.model_manifest_trust. No production trust anchor for that manifest is published (WP-00 binding ledger row 13; gates G-3a and G-3b), so installation_catalogue composes an empty installable catalogue, a production admission establishes no capacity requirement, and the deferral cannot arise on a production installation. The cited admission evidence reaches it with a manifest signed and verified under the dev/test anchor its own environment flag unlocks, which proves the path carries declared sizes end to end but is not the owner's authority.
gates.limitations: Eviction, its exclusions -- pinned, leased and unverified -- the shortest-prefix victim order, the deferral and the intactness of the pins and the cap are covered against the production lifecycle, across two processes. The admission reservation is sized against the requested sets' declared byte_size, excludes already-installed members from both the requirement and the candidates, and runs inside the same coordination block as the inventory read it decides on. Further tests beyond those cited cover the inclusive boundary, the lease and divergence exclusions, the free-capacity shortcut, an absent cache, retry after a pin is released and the identity usage fault. The in-flight half runs over a real capture runner through production admission, outbox, replay, settlement and a real restart. Three limits remain. The 512 MiB cap is reached by declaring a large byte_size rather than writing it, and that filler has no bytes, so it is never a victim. Model payloads are stand-in bytes pinned by real digests, not Tesseract data. And the native surface that would display the required capacity is not in this repository, so what is covered is the contract it reads and not its display.

gates.normative_summary: A new source capture races reprocessing of an older capture. The independent source and extraction heads remain correct, and reprocessing an old source cannot make that old source current.
gates.applicability: The Core canonical source and extraction head boundary on every OS the runtime supports.

evidence.covers: The source and extraction heads cannot move in one write, which is what keeps them independent.
Work against an older base stays historical and never becomes current.
A completion arriving after a newer one is superseded rather than winning.
Reprocessing against a stale expected head is historical, so the old source cannot be made current through it.
A legitimate reprocess publishes from retained bytes, which is the case the refusals must not break.

gates.limitations: Core side only, in a single process against the real SQLite store and ServiceRunner. The race is sequenced deterministically by each test rather than run concurrently, so the head invariants are proven over commit order and not under genuine contention between a capture and a reprocess worker. No companion or scheduler participates.

gates.normative_summary: Mixed ordinary files and multiple folder modes. Each reviewed group has its own confirmation and receipt, and one group cannot silently submit another or claim whole-collection atomicity.
gates.applicability: macOS 13 or later companion review draft holding ordinary files alongside more than one folder group.

evidence.covers: Each group is confirmed and receipted independently, in any order.
Confirming one folder never submits the pending files or the other folder.
Confirming the files never submits a pending folder.
One failed group does not fail or cancel the others, which refutes whole-collection atomicity.
Cancelling one folder is reported for that folder alone.
A restart keeps each confirmed group durable and restores only the unconfirmed ones.
A folder is never published with, or blocking, the ordinary files beside it.

gates.limitations: Unsigned swift test process on the macos-latest runner, OS and Xcode versions unrecorded. Groups are assembled in-test rather than arriving from real pickers, drops or extensions, the delivery client is a fake, and the restart is a store reopen rather than a process relaunch. The receipts are checked as records, not as rendered UI.

gates.normative_summary: Upgrade from v1 native access and the v2 mailbox, then downgrade. Original requests preserve their exact canonical request and keys and acquire no watch consent, and unknown full-solution schemas are preserved and blocked.
gates.applicability: macOS 13 or later companion across a forward migration of the access store and the handoff mailbox, and a subsequent rollback.

evidence.covers: The v1 per-member access layout migrates forward to one root grant.
A contradictory legacy record fails closed rather than being resolved by guesswork.
A v1 interrupted attempt migrates without inventing a new identity, which preserves the exact request and keys.
An unknown newer schema is blocked and its bytes are preserved.
A prior v1 publication is recovered as an explicitly legacy unresolved intent rather than being reinterpreted.

A v1 access store is upgraded and rolled back: every grant keeps its reference, document, generation and route, the migrated root group holds no owner, cannot enumerate and cannot enrol a sibling (no watch consent), and both a section the build does not define under a known schema name and an unknown schema name are refused whole with the bytes untouched.

A v1 queue manifest is upgraded and rolled back: the queued request keeps its item, canonical digest, operation key and the attempt key derived from it, and a newer entry field or a newer schema name is refused with the bytes untouched.
An offer from a newer mailbox schema is refused on decode and the offer already held is left exactly as written.
A newer schema's offer sitting in the mailbox is not returned as pending and is not deleted, with its snapshots, by the pending-offer sweep.
A scheduling document under a newer schema name is refused and left byte for byte as it was.
A scheduling document with a section this build does not define under its own schema name is refused whole rather than read as a subset and rewritten.

gates.limitations: Executed and passing on 2026-10-16 as unsigned swift test cases. A downgrade is never a second build: the current reader is the older reader, and the newer install is simulated by writing the documents a later full solution would leave, in both shapes it can take (an undefined section under a known schema name, and an unknown schema name). The round trip is proven per store (access, queue, mailbox, scheduling) rather than as one combined fixture. The stores refuse a document's unknown top-level keys; an unknown field inside an individual native-access record or handoff offer is still read as a subset.

gates.normative_summary: Full prototype and native handoff coverage. Every complete-solution capability maps to a real implementation package and to acceptance evidence, and simulated UI results are clearly separated from native, Core and parser proof.
gates.applicability: The whole complete-solution capability set. This is the meta-gate WP-15 itself answers, and this ledger is the artefact that answers it.

evidence.covers: The mapping itself: every gate in section 20 with its applicability, its evidence class, its repository evidence, a result and the exact condition still missing.
The closed schema that keeps the mapping's shape, its status vocabulary and its evidence vocabulary from drifting.
The deterministic gate that rejects a missing or duplicate gate, an unknown status, a stale or nonexistent evidence reference, and a passed gate without supporting evidence.
The fail-closed proof that the checker rejects each of those defects rather than passing by accident.
The human-readable status generated from the ledger, with counts by family and by status.

gates.missing_condition: The mapping this gate requires now exists and is enforced, but the gate requires every capability to map to acceptance evidence, and most gates in this ledger do not have it. The separation clause is also only partly met: the evidence_type vocabulary separates repository tests from installed-build, real-host, accessibility and external-fixture evidence, but no simulated UI or prototype result is recorded anywhere, so there is nothing yet to separate on that axis.
gates.limitations: This gate cannot be met by its own artefact. The ledger makes the coverage auditable and makes a false claim of qualification fail the build; it does not itself constitute the acceptance evidence the other 129 gates need.
